title: One billion meals thrown away every day
speaker: Breaking News English (Sean Banville)

keyTerms.definition: when many people in a place have no food
the people who live together in one home
a place where rubbish is buried
a gas that traps heat and warms the planet

predictionQuestion: How much food do you think the world throws away? Who wastes the most: homes, restaurants or shops?

keyIdeas.text: More than a billion meals are wasted every day, even though some people are starving.
Homes cause most food waste: about 60 per cent.
Restaurants and food services waste about 28 per cent, and shops about 12 per cent.
The Maldives has the highest home food waste per person (about 260 kg a year).
Food waste causes about 8 to 10 per cent of the world's greenhouse gas emissions.
Rotting food in landfill releases gases like methane, which speeds up global warming.
People, businesses and governments can all take steps to reduce food waste.
Tips for people: plan meals, use a shopping list, buy only what you need, store and freeze food, and reuse leftovers.
Restaurants and supermarkets can give extra food to people in need.
Less waste would save money, improve food security and help with climate change.

questions.stem: According to the report, who is responsible for most food waste?
questions.explanation: Homes are responsible for about 60 per cent of food waste.

questions.stem: About how much of the world's greenhouse gas emissions comes from food waste?
questions.explanation: The report gives 8 to 10 per cent. The other numbers are shares of food waste, not emissions.

questions.stem: Why is food in landfill a problem for the climate?
options: As it rots, it releases gases like methane
It takes up too much space
questions.answer: As it rots, it releases gases like methane
questions.explanation: Rotting food releases greenhouse gases such as methane, which speeds up global warming.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the tips for households?
options: Buy food in bulk to save money
questions.answer: Buy food in bulk to save money
questions.explanation: The advice is to buy only what you need, not to buy more.

questions.stem: What can restaurants and supermarkets do?
options: Give extra food to people in need
Sell food only in small packets
questions.answer: Give extra food to people in need
questions.explanation: They can donate surplus food to people who need it.
